guidance.procedure: After deciding the relation, collect every complete responsive member: the operative sentence plus any governing lead-in, definition introduction, exception introduction, or continuation needed to express its force, actor, object, trigger, or scope. Include repeated provisions that independently resolve the hypothesis. Exclude headings, neighboring examples, generic security or duration language, and clauses that are merely useful context.

Inspect the disclosure prohibition together with its exceptions and the identity of permitted recipients. A pattern such as “do not disclose except to necessary agents, consultants, or advisers” supports sharing some information with some third parties. A ban followed only by access for the recipient’s employees or officers opposes third-party sharing; a bare ban with no responsive exception also opposes it. Do not treat employees alone as third parties.

Evaluate possession after the required return or destruction is completed. An express archival, backup, legal, dispute, or other retention exception supports permissible post-return possession. A requirement to return or destroy all information or copies, with no retention carve-out, opposes it; choosing destruction instead of return does not imply that something may remain. A return duty alone does not become permission merely because possession existed before the trigger.

Match the return-or-destroy trigger to termination of the agreement or relationship. “Upon termination, return or destroy” supports the hypothesis. “Upon request” or “upon demand” alone does not, even if placed in a return section or even if the agreement can separately terminate; it supports the hypothesis only when the request duty is expressly tied to termination. Do not substitute transaction abandonment or an unrelated trigger without textual linkage.

Look for obligations that expressly continue, survive, remain enforceable, or are not released after termination or expiration. A fixed agreement term, an effective-date duration, or language that the agreement remains in force is not by itself an obligation-survival provision. If the text affirmatively ends the relevant duties at termination or confines them to the agreement term, it opposes survival; otherwise duration language without a post-termination link leaves the hypothesis unresolved.

Test the word “only” against the operative confidential-information definition or deeming provisions. Express inclusion of business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, contractual, or similarly nontechnical information contradicts a technical-only definition. A definition expressly confined to technical information supports it. Generic breadth such as “all information” or background discussion of commercial material, without an operative identifiable nontechnical category, does not automatically settle the proposition.

Because the hypothesis concerns all confidential information, verify whether identification or marking is a universal condition, including any oral-information procedure. A clause protecting information whether or not labeled, or protecting information merely because a reasonable person would understand it as confidential, opposes universal express identification. A broad definition with no marking rule is unresolved, not automatically contradictory; cite the complete marking sequence when it is the governing condition.

Require the definition or disclosure rule to cover communication mode. Express references to oral, spoken, verbal, visual, or a comprehensive tangible/intangible disclosure formulation support inclusion of verbally conveyed information. A clause about discussions, agreement content, or information existing “in any form” inside a subject-matter list does not necessarily establish oral disclosure. If the contract addresses content but not conveyance mode, use NotMentioned rather than inference.

An exclusion or exception for information independently developed without use of or access to protected information supports permissible independent development; include the exception’s governing lead-in as well as the specific limb when both carry its legal force. A nondisclosure, nonuse, or copying prohibition does not prohibit independent development by implication. Without an express development rule or an actual opposing prohibition, the issue is unresolved.

A definition exclusion or exception for information lawfully received from an unrestricted third-party source supports acquiring similar information from a third party. Include the governing exclusion lead-in and any conditions identifying the lawful, nonconfidential source. A ban on disclosing the current confidential information says nothing about acquiring other information and therefore is not contradiction. Do not infer permission solely from a public-domain or independent-development exception.

Distinguish express permission from prohibition. “May copy only as reasonably necessary for the stated purpose” supports permissible copying; “shall not copy” or “shall not copy without prior consent” opposes it. A general right to use information does not itself grant copying, and a general nondisclosure duty does not itself prohibit copying. When the operative copy rule follows a lead-in identifying the recipient’s undertakings, include both if needed for actor and force.

Separate permission to comply with law from a duty to notify. Entailment requires language obligating the receiving party to give notice, an opportunity to object, or equivalent warning when disclosure is legally compelled. A compelled-disclosure exception without notice leaves the notice hypothesis unresolved. For evidence, include any governing exception lead-in and the operative notice provision, but exclude a generic legal-disclosure permission unless it is part of that condition.

Find an express allowance for disclosure or access to the receiving party’s employees, ordinarily conditioned on need to know or the stated purpose. Such an allowance supports sharing with some employees even when general disclosure is prohibited. Permission only for outside advisers does not establish employee sharing. A bare third-party nondisclosure or no-copy clause, without addressing employees, leaves employee sharing unresolved rather than opposing it.

Support limited use with provisions that actually restrict use to the stated purpose or forbid every other use, including a governing purpose clause when it supplies the operative limit. Include repeated independently operative nonuse provisions. Do not cite confidentiality, security, disclosure, copying, survival, or no-license language merely because it is nearby; those provisions are members only if they themselves impose the hypothesis’s use limitation.

Treat an express denial of any license, title, right of use, or other interest in the confidential information as support. Property-retention language is responsive only when it independently denies the recipient a right, not merely because it names the owner. Where a sentence begins with a construction formula and continues into a subordinate no-right provision, include the complete linked provision; include separate no-license clauses when each independently resolves the hypothesis.

Match the duty to an ending event, not merely the word “termination.” Return or destruction triggered by termination or expiration, conclusion of services or a project, ending discussions, abandoning the contemplated transaction, or a scheduled final-return deadline after the agreement term supports the hypothesis. A request-only duty during an otherwise continuing relationship is unresolved. Include the ending-event language and every operative return/destruction limb.

operations.rationale: The prior exact-termination rule correctly rejected request-only clauses but caused negative transfer where annotations treated conclusion of the engagement, abandoned negotiations, project completion, or a final post-term deadline as the relevant termination event.

guidance.procedure: Evaluate what may remain after the stated return or destruction is completed. An express archive, backup, legal-retention, dispute, or records exception supports possession. An exhaustive duty covering all protected information and all copies, or an express no-retention sentence, opposes it. A duty covering only tangible documents or another specified subset, without saying nothing else may remain, is unresolved. Thus “return all records and copies; retain none” opposes, while “return tangible materials” alone does not.

operations.rationale: The former rule overgeneralized every unqualified return clause into contradiction, producing harm on a clause limited to tangible materials, while also failing to make the exhaustive-versus-partial object boundary executable.

guidance.procedure: Inspect the operative protected-information definition, including a recital that directly declares the defined object. A formulation such as “the technical information described below is Confidential Information” supports technical-only coverage even without repeating “only.” Express business, financial, commercial, personnel, customer, or similar nontechnical categories oppose it. Mere background that parties possess technical or commercial material, or a generic definition such as “all information” without an identifiable content category, leaves the proposition unresolved.

operations.rationale: The existing generic-breadth warning did not prevent false contradictions on content-neutral definitions and contributed to reversing the technical-only relation where a recital directly defined the protected information as technical.

guidance.procedure: Test whether every protected item must be affirmatively identified to the recipient. Marking, contemporaneous designation, later written confirmation, or the discloser expressly making the recipient aware can support the universal condition. Coverage “whether or not marked,” or based only on what a reasonable recipient should understand, opposes it. A broad definition, an authority’s general classification scheme, or the discloser merely considering information confidential does not itself communicate an identification for every disclosure and is unresolved. Include the complete governing identification sequence.

operations.rationale: Current answers confused general classification or broad confidentiality with communicated identification, while also treating an express made-aware alternative as defeating rather than satisfying identification.

guidance.procedure: Require an operative statement about conveyance mode. “Information transmitted verbally, in writing, or electronically,” when it defines the protected object, supports oral coverage, as do explicit oral, spoken, or verbal terms and comprehensive tangible/intangible formulations. References merely to discussions, information learned, agreement content, or information “in any form” within a subject-matter list do not establish verbal disclosure. If oral protection depends on designation or written confirmation, include the responsive condition sequence.

operations.rationale: The prior rule correctly rejected discussion-based inference but was ignored on an express verbally-transmitted definition; the worked contrast makes that boundary operational without broadening mere conversational references.

guidance.procedure: Require a specific independent-development provision, ordinarily stating development without use of, reference to, or access to protected information. A generic exclusions lead-in is responsive evidence only when paired with that particular limb. Public-domain, third-party-source, compelled-disclosure, nondisclosure, nonuse, or copying language alone neither permits nor prohibits independent development and leaves the issue unresolved. A direct ban on independent development would oppose the hypothesis.

operations.rationale: The lawyer treated a generic exception introduction and unrelated restrictions as independent-development rules in the new batch, despite the existing broad warning.

guidance.procedure: Look for an incoming-source rule: information may be received, obtained, furnished, or acquired from a lawful third party not bound by confidentiality or other transmission restrictions. Pair the specific source limb with its governing exclusion introduction and stated conditions. A generic exception introduction, a legal-demand clause, an outgoing third-party disclosure rule, or an independent-development limb does not address acquisition and is unresolved. For example, “received from an unrestricted outside source” supports; “may disclose when compelled” does not.

operations.rationale: Skills changed correct unresolved answers into entailments by copying generic exception or compelled-disclosure text that never addressed incoming acquisition.

guidance.procedure: Distinguish permission, a blanket ban, and a restriction on copying manner. “May copy” or “shall not copy except as necessary” supports; an unqualified “shall not copy” opposes. A rule only forbidding copies that obscure markings, or regulating the form or handling of copies, leaves general permission unresolved. If one grammatical exception governs a series such as “do not copy or disclose except to necessary employees,” it can support copying within that exception. Include the undertaking lead-in when it supplies actor or force.

operations.rationale: The earlier binary rule caused qualified copy-handling restrictions to be treated as blanket prohibitions and did not explain when a shared grammatical exception can authorize copying.

guidance.procedure: Find both legal compulsion and mandatory warning. A pattern such as “when disclosure is required by law, notify the discloser before releasing the information” supports the hypothesis even without a separately labeled compelled-disclosure exception. Permission to comply with law without notice is unresolved. Include the trigger and notice sentence; when the notice is a proviso referring to listed legal processes, include the governing lead-in and all referenced limbs needed to identify the compelled event, but omit unrelated disclosure permissions.

operations.rationale: The lawyer missed a direct pre-release notice duty and repeatedly selected only the final notice fragment from longer compelled-disclosure conditions.

guidance.procedure: Read the operative ban, its exceptions, recipient definitions, and access obligations together. Authorization for consultants, agents, advisers, contractors, affiliates, or other representatives supports sharing with some third parties; access language covering agents or representatives may complete an employee exception. Employee/officer-only access followed by a ban on everyone else opposes it, as does a bare outside-recipient ban. Merely describing a signer as an employee or agent, or the owner directly granting that individual access, does not authorize the receiving party and leaves the hypothesis unresolved.

operations.rationale: The former rule was not executable enough: answers still treated employee-only access as outside sharing, copied recipient-status provisions, and missed permissions reaching consultants or other representatives.

guidance.procedure: Require an operative allowance for the receiving party to disclose or provide access to its employees, usually subject to need-to-know or purpose limits. A statement that a designated signer happens to be an employee, officer, agent, or consultant describes status rather than authorizing the receiving party to share and leaves the issue unresolved. Permission only for outside advisers does not establish employee sharing; a general disclosure ban without an employee exception also remains unresolved unless it expressly covers and forbids employees.

operations.rationale: The lawyer continued to infer employee-sharing permission from the status of an already authorized individual; a compact status-versus-authorization distinction addresses the observed failure.

guidance.procedure: Separate agreement duration from the duration of substantive duties. “These duties survive termination” supports survival. “The agreement remains effective for five years” alone is unresolved. A clause confining the confidentiality or use duties themselves to a fixed period from the effective date, with no post-termination continuation, opposes survival; for example, “the confidentiality obligations extend only five years from signing.” Enforcement, indemnity, severability, or remedy language does not become survival merely because it can be invoked later.

operations.rationale: The earlier rule was broadly correct but did not stop a fixed-duration confidentiality duty from being labeled survival, while the new batch confirmed the need to exclude remedies and enforcement provisions.

guidance.procedure: Collect every provision that independently limits use to the stated purpose or forbids other use, including a governing purpose clause and repeated nonuse provisions. Exclude headings, disclosure/security duties, and a pure ownership or no-license clause. However, a construction clause stating that no license exists except a limited right to use solely for the stated purpose independently expresses the use limit and is responsive. After finding one restriction, scan the whole contract for a second operative restriction rather than stopping at the first candidate.

operations.rationale: Use relations remained stable, but evidence repeatedly omitted independent purpose restrictions and a linked no-license formulation that expressly preserved only the purpose-limited use right.

guidance.procedure: Support the hypothesis with an express denial of license, title, proprietary right, right of use, or other interest. A limited permission to review or use information for the stated purpose does not by itself oppose this no-proprietary-right proposition. Sole-and-exclusive ownership coupled with mandatory return can independently deny the recipient an interest; mere identification of the owner cannot. Include a linked construction lead-in and subordinate denial, and include each separate clause that independently denies rights.

operations.rationale: The existing rule successfully prevented several false contradictions, but evidence still omitted separate ownership-based denials; the revision preserves that gain while making the limited-use and exclusive-ownership boundaries explicit.

guidance.procedure: Inspect whether the agreement’s existence, negotiation, terms, content, discussions, or expressly designated subject matter is itself confidential or non-disclosable. Such language supports the hypothesis. A generic entire-agreement clause, confidentiality of exchanged business information, or a reference to discussions that does not protect their existence leaves it unresolved. Express authorization to disclose the fact of the agreement would oppose it. Include the definition lead-in when it is what makes agreement terms or negotiations protected.

operations.rationale: The library lacked a scoped procedure for the sole recurring relation error, and the new batch missed an express provision treating the agreement’s subject matter as confidential.

guidance.procedure: Look for an operative prohibition on soliciting, recruiting, hiring, inducing departure, or otherwise approaching specified representatives of the disclosing party. A targeted no-contact or non-circumvention clause covering employees or other associated persons also supports the benchmark proposition when it forbids approaching them in connection with the contemplated transaction. General nondisclosure, noncompetition, or restrictions concerning customers or markets alone are unresolved. Include any lead-in supplying the actor, protected class, or duration.

operations.rationale: No scoped rule addressed solicitation, and the current memory answer lost a correct relation by overlooking an annotated employee no-contact/non-circumvention prohibition.
